fact: The government is advancing its data exchange interoperability platform, launched on 22 April 2025, with phase one due by end of December 2025 and a COCOOR meeting having validated the roadmap (as_of is the publication date, the meeting being undated).
The ministry with JICA launched on 22 April 2025 an interministerial interoperable data-sharing platform project, with a pilot phase planned 2024-2025 and large-scale deployment 2025-2027.

MCTN/PAENS called on 24 September 2026 for expressions of interest, closing 7 October 2026, to study infrastructure needs of the future X-Road-based national interoperability platform PINS, financed by a World Bank IDA credit.

The ministry announced a 5 May 2026 session presenting the draft decree governing the interoperability platform and the data exchange architectures, while stating that state information systems still run in silos that communicate little.

The project coordination committee met in the week of 15 September 2025, validated the roadmap and the ministry said phase one would be delivered at end December 2025; the platform was launched 22 April 2025 with pilot 2024-2025 and scale-up 2025-2027.

A government presenter at the WSIS Forum 2026 session said the X-Road based interoperability platform PINs has had an MVP 1.0 launched with two use cases, social protection and public finance; the document gives no launch date, so its published date is used.

The platform's own portal describes the Plateforme d'Interoperabilite du Senegal (e-Jokkoo, built on X-Road) as connecting state information systems for secure data exchange between administrations, with API Gateway, Identite Numerique and Data Exchange services listed; its counters for connected administrations, active APIs and monthly transactions show only placeholders, and the page gives no date, so its published date is used.

The ministry, with JICA, is implementing an interministerial interoperable data exchange platform on X-Road, now in a pilot phase with one use case linking the RNU, SIGICMU, civil status and national identity card systems; extension to more ministries is planned.
